So, what's the best magic system you've read about in fantasy?

Favorite I've read so far is in Mistborn. Sanderson came up with a system that allows for a person to channel an epic amount of power while still satisfying conservation of energy (well enough to be believed, anyhow). Some characters can "burn metal", consuming the metal for energy for their magic. It's nice to not wonder why the society hasn't harnessed unlimited energy for industrial use.

Well, the answer to the last question is probably simply that the Lord Ruler was deliberately suppressing any such industrial tendencies. It seems to be implied that the trend is reversed in Alloy of Law, though.
The Lord Ruler did suppress industry, but even when you see industry in the Wax & Wayne book, you don't see industry powered by free magical energy.

You do see things like Rioter/Soother therapists and Feruchemist researchers. I think it's a safe bet that more than likely, we'll see Allomancy used in this capacity in some way as the future books explain what the post-Lord Ruler world looks like. We'll have to wait and see, I suppose.

Probably the One Power in The Wheel of Time. There was such an incredible sense of wonder and mystery as you saw it all through the lens of mythology and folklore. Yet Jordan takes the time to establish a sense of rationality and history. The world feels like one that has been shaped by this power's presence, and the rules are just detailed enough that they impart a sense of believability.

When you take the time to think about it, the system isn't as "functional" as the magic in, say, Mistborn or The Name of the Wind. In those books, you can think about a situation and actually infer what would happen under the rules as they have been so far defined. But few stories have matched the feel he created for the One Power. When you read about it, you don't think, "Oh, that's his magic system," you think, "This is the One Power." It feels thoroughly it's own thing, completely original, and it evokes a powerful sense that there's so much more than you get to see.
I was actually impressed by the system in the Paolini's Inheritance Cycle.
